story_type: thrusters fail on a docked crew capsule, rescue rocket readied, 1973 mission film
hook: Their thrusters were failing. NASA started readying a rescue.
narration: Their steering thrusters were failing, and NASA started getting a rescue ready.
July 1973. Alan Bean, Owen Garriott and Jack Lousma launched for the longest spaceflight yet.
Almost eight hours after liftoff, they caught up with the Skylab space station and docked.
But an oxidizer leak had shown up in one of the thruster quads on their Apollo command module.
On mission day six, a second thruster quad indicated failure.
Those thrusters aim the capsule. Lose too many, and holding it steady for the fall home gets harder.
As a precaution, rescue plans were set in motion, and work on a rescue vehicle was sped up.
Analysis showed the capsule's backup control modes were more than adequate to come home.
[short pause] By mid September, it was clear the rescue would not be flown.
outcome: After two months in space, the crew splashed down off Southern California, and the rescue mission was never needed.
title: Thrusters failing, rescue rocket readied
description:
During the second Skylab mission in 1973, two thruster quads on the crew's Apollo command module leaked or failed, and NASA set rescue plans in motion. Analysis showed the backup controls were adequate, and the crew returned after two months. From the NASA film Skylab: The Second Manned Mission.
